name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 20
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 20

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of combined deficiency of multiple respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Presence of multisystem involvement including neurological and muscular symptoms consistent with mitochondrial disease
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes affecting mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia or brainstem abnormalities supportive of mitochondrial dysfunction
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial respiratory chain dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of combined respiratory chain enzyme deficiency plus clinical features consistent with mitochondrial disease and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of biochemical, clinical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated lactate levels due to mitochondrial dysfunction
Generalized decreased muscle tone and strength
searchTerms: muscle weakness with low muscle tone

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Hearing impairment due to cochlear or nerve involvement

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver due to metabolic stress

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate
Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV in muscle biopsy
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia lesions and cerebral atrophy
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrating lactate peak
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation proteins (e.g., NDUFS1, SURF1)
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions may be present
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated complex I deficiency rather than combined defects
Characteristic symmetric necrotic lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem
Usually associated with specific mitochondrial or nuclear gene mutations

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurological deterioration in infancy
Refractory lactic acidosis despite supportive care
Multisystem involvement including cardiomyopathy and respiratory failure
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease: clinical features and diagnosis. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2020;43(1):1-12.
